mutant.description: Leases are run-scoped but queue entries are still matched by task id: a sibling's queue entry blocks.

tests.name: 1. same task id, different runs: each run is confirmed against its own permit only
2. same task id, different providers: a codex run does not block a gemini cancel, and the reverse
3. same task id, same provider: a sibling run's permit AND queue entry never block, a run's own always do
tests.error: B's queue entry is not A's: [{"kind":"lease","holder":"fake:model:T:pid75777:run=run-A","pid":75777,"run":"run-A"},{"kind":"waiter","holder":"fake:model:T:pid75777:run=run-B","pid":75777,"run":"run-B"}] 2 !== 1

tests.name: 4. missing or default provider: a task with no provider is confirmed on its own permit, not a foreign one
5. injected handle / resource mismatch can neither hide the target's permit nor adopt a foreign one
6. target permit still active: STOPPED is never reported, however terminal the run looks
7. target process still active: a provider call that outlived its abort keeps the permit, and the cancel waits for it
8a. cancellation while queued for the permit: nothing is held, and no permit is taken later
8b. cancellation landing right after the permit is granted, before the call: the permit is released and the cancel is confirmed
9a. lease expiry: a crashed, un-renewed permit blocks while live and stops blocking when it expires
9b. recovery: a re-run of the same task is not blocked by the previous run's stale permit, and the previous run still is
10. unknown or legacy ownership fails closed for every run, for permits and for queue entries
10b. an unreadable ownership marker is unknown ownership, not "some other run" (pins the holder syntax, see the header)
11. the Mastra workflow carries its own run id into the permit it takes (scheduler -> workflow run -> capacity)
12. overlapping run ids never match each other (whole-value comparison, not substring or prefix)
13. the runner's own retry takes a second permit for the SAME run, and that permit carries the run id too

14. scheduler -> executor -> workflow: the run id the scheduler stores is the one that owns the permit, so a foreign run of the same task never blocks the scheduler's own cancel and an unattributable permit still does
a permit nobody can attribute to a run, held on ANOTHER resource than the probe's, still blocks (http-boundary.test.ts:132 in miniature)
